faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: Quick answers about creating lists, sharing with guests, and keeping claims private.

items.question: Do guests need to create an account?
items.answer: No. Guests open the shared list link, pick a gift, and enter their name. No sign-up required.

items.question: Can guests see who claimed each gift?
items.answer: No. Guests only see whether an item is available or already selected. Only the list host sees claimer names.

items.question: Which stores can I import products from?
items.answer: Paste a link from most online stores. Amazon and Next are supported with dedicated parsers; other sites use standard product metadata when available.

items.question: What if a product link fails to import?
items.answer: Some retailers block automated fetching. Try the direct product page URL, or add the item details manually after creating the list.

items.question: Can a guest unclaim a gift?
items.answer: Yes. From the same browser they used to claim, they can unclaim their selection. The gift becomes available again for others.

items.question: Can the host claim a gift on behalf of someone?
items.answer: Yes. From the manage view, hosts can claim items on behalf of a guest — useful when coordinating in person or by phone.

items.question: How do I share my list with guests?
items.answer: Copy the guest link from your manage page and send it by text, email, or invitation. Guests use that link — not the manage URL.

items.question: Do lists update in real time?
items.answer: Yes. When someone claims or unclaims a gift, other open list pages update automatically without refreshing.

items.question: Can I export my list after the event?
items.answer: Yes. Hosts can export a PDF from the manage page with every item, claim status, guest name, and claim date — handy for thank-you notes.

items.question: Is WishGather free?
items.answer: Yes. Create a list, share it with guests, and manage claims at no cost.

items.question: How is WishGather different from a shared spreadsheet?
items.answer: Spreadsheets show every edit to everyone and are easy to break. WishGather gives guests a simple claim flow, hides names from other guests, and updates in real time — no version conflicts.

items.question: Can I use WishGather instead of a store registry?
items.answer: Yes. Add gifts from any store by link or manually. You keep full control and privacy without tying your list to one retailer.

items.question: How do I make a gift list guests will actually use?
items.answer: Keep items clear, share one guest link, and let people claim gifts privately. Our Gift List guide on WishGather walks through planning, sharing, and updates step by step.

giftRegistry.title: A free online gift registry that keeps guest claims private
giftRegistry.lead: WishGather helps you build a beautiful wish list for any celebration. Share one link, let guests claim gifts without accounts, and see who picked what — while other guests only see what's still available.

sections.title: Why hosts choose WishGather
sections.body: Traditional registries lock you into one store. Shared spreadsheets expose every name and duplicate gift. WishGather is a privacy-first gift registry: guests get a clean mobile page, you get a host dashboard with live updates, and nobody sees each other's choices.

sections.title: Add gifts from anywhere
sections.body: Paste a product URL from Amazon, Next, or most online shops and we pull title, image, and price when possible. You can always edit details or add items manually — perfect for experiences, cash funds, or local boutiques.

sections.title: One link for every guest
sections.body: Copy the guest link from your manage page and drop it in invitations, group chats, or email. Guests claim in seconds with no sign-up. If plans change, they can unclaim from the same browser and the gift opens back up instantly.

faqs.question: Is WishGather really free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Creating a registry, sharing with guests, and managing claims costs nothing.

faqs.question: Do guests need an account?
faqs.answer: No. They open your guest link, choose a gift, and enter their name.

faqs.question: Can I use this for weddings and showers?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Many hosts use WishGather for baby showers, birthdays, weddings, and housewarmings.

babyShowerRegistry.title: Baby shower gift registry with private guest claims
babyShowerRegistry.lead: Collect exactly what you need for baby — without duplicate onesies or awkward spreadsheet rows. WishGather keeps shower guests aligned while protecting everyone's privacy.

sections.title: Built for shower guests on their phones
sections.body: Most shower guests shop from a text message link on mobile. WishGather loads fast, shows clear Available badges, and makes claiming a gift a two-tap flow — no app install and no account.

sections.title: You see names; guests do not
sections.body: Only you, the host, see who claimed each item. Other guests see Available or Already Selected, which prevents pile-ons and keeps the surprise for thank-you notes.

sections.title: Mix registry staples and boutique finds
sections.body: Add big-box links, Etsy finds, or hand-entered items like diaper service credits. Import helpers fetch product details when retailers allow it; everything else is a quick manual add.

faqs.question: Can co-hosts manage the same list?
faqs.answer: Share your host login credentials with a trusted co-host, or coordinate from one manage screen during the shower.

faqs.question: What if two people claim the same gift?
faqs.answer: Claims update in real time. Once an item is selected, others see it as unavailable immediately.

faqs.question: Can I export thank-you data?
faqs.answer: Yes. Export a PDF from manage with item, guest name, and claim date.

birthdayWishList.title: Birthday wish list your guests will actually use
birthdayWishList.lead: Skip the group chat chaos. Publish a birthday wish list with photos and prices, share one link, and let friends claim gifts privately so you avoid duplicates.

sections.title: Perfect for kids' parties and milestone birthdays
sections.body: Parents love clear lists for classmates; adults love linking favorite brands or experiences. WishGather works for both — one registry tool for every age.

sections.title: Guests stay anonymous to each other
sections.body: Friends see what's left to buy, not who already bought it. You still get full visibility to plan the party and write thank-you notes.

sections.title: Update anytime before the party
sections.body: Add last-minute ideas from your manage page. Guests' open tabs refresh automatically when something new is claimed or released.

faqs.question: Can guests shop anywhere?
faqs.answer: Yes. Add links from any store or describe an item manually. Guests buy off-site and mark the gift claimed on your list.

faqs.question: Is there an age limit?
faqs.answer: No. Hosts must create an account, but guests of any age can claim with a name.

faqs.question: Does it work for surprise parties?
faqs.answer: Yes. Share the guest link only with people who should see the list; keep your manage URL private.

giftList.title: Gift List: How to Create and Share the Perfect Gift Wishlist
giftList.lead: A great gift list helps guests buy confidently without duplicate presents. This guide walks through planning, sharing, and managing a gift list (or wishlist) that works on phones, keeps claims private, and stays easy to update until the big day.

sections.title: What is a gift list?
sections.body: A gift list — sometimes called a wishlist or registry — is a single place where you collect ideas for presents you would love to receive. Unlike a scattered group chat or spreadsheet, a dedicated gift list shows photos, prices, and what is still available. When guests can claim items privately, everyone avoids buying the same thing twice.

sections.title: Step 1: Plan before you publish
sections.body: Start with the event in mind: birthday party, baby shower, wedding, or holiday. Aim for a mix of price points so every guest can participate. Group similar items, note sizes or colors if they matter, and leave a few open slots for last-minute ideas. A focused gift list of 10–25 items is easier for guests to scan than an endless catalog.

sections.title: Step 2: Add gifts with clear details
sections.body: For each entry on your gift list, include a short title, optional photo, and link to the store when you have one. WishGather can import product details from many URLs so your gift list looks polished without manual copy-paste. If a link fails, add the item manually — clarity matters more than perfect automation.

sections.title: Step 3: Share one guest link
sections.body: Send the public gift list URL — not your private manage link — in invitations, email, or text. One link keeps everyone on the same version of the list. Ask guests to claim what they plan to buy so the gift list updates in real time and others see what is still available.

sections.title: Step 4: Keep the gift list alive until the event
sections.body: Add items as you think of them, and remind guests that unclaimed gifts are still up for grabs. After the celebration, export a summary for thank-you notes. A well-maintained gift list reduces stress for you and makes shopping simpler for everyone who cares about you.

faqs.question: Gift list vs wishlist — is there a difference?
faqs.answer: People use the terms interchangeably. A gift list usually emphasizes items others can buy for you; a wishlist can include dreams or experiences. WishGather supports both — add products, notes, or flexible ideas in one place.

faqs.question: How many items should my gift list include?
faqs.answer: Enough variety that guests find something in their budget, but not so many that the list feels overwhelming. Many hosts land between 12 and 30 items depending on guest count.

faqs.question: Should guests see each other's names on the gift list?
faqs.answer: On WishGather, only the host sees claimer names. Guests see Available or Already Selected, which keeps the gift list friendly and private.

faqs.question: Can I use a gift list for a virtual party?
faqs.answer: Yes. Share the link digitally; guests can shop online and mark items claimed from anywhere.

giftWishlist.title: Why Create a Gift Wishlist?
giftWishlist.lead: A gift wishlist is more than a shopping list — it is a friendly way to tell people what you would love to receive. Whether you call it a wishlist, gift list, or registry, sharing curated ideas helps guests choose thoughtfully, saves everyone time, and cuts down on duplicate or unwanted gifts.

sections.title: Avoid unwanted gifts
sections.body: Without a wishlist, guests guess — and well-meaning surprises do not always match your taste or needs. A clear gift wishlist steers people toward items you actually want, from the right size and color to experiences you have been hoping for. You stay gracious; they stay confident.

sections.title: Make gift shopping easier
sections.body: Hunting for ideas is the hardest part of buying a present. When you publish a gift wishlist with links, photos, and prices, shoppers skip the scroll and go straight to checkout. That is especially helpful for busy friends, family abroad, or anyone shopping from a phone between meetings.

sections.title: Share your preferences
sections.body: Your wishlist reflects your personality — favorite brands, hobbies, and little luxuries you would never buy for yourself. Sharing a gift wishlist is softer than sending a direct hint, and it gives guests room to pick something that still feels personal within your guidelines.

sections.title: Organize gift ideas in one place
sections.body: Screenshots, bookmarks, and chat threads scatter fast. A single gift wishlist keeps every idea together, easy to update, and simple to share with one link. Add items as inspiration strikes, remove what you have already bought yourself, and let guests see what is still available.

faqs.question: Is a gift wishlist the same as a registry?
faqs.answer: Often yes in practice. Registries are common for weddings and baby showers; a gift wishlist works for birthdays, holidays, and any event where you want guests to see curated ideas in one place.

faqs.question: Will a wishlist feel impersonal?
faqs.answer: Not when you mix price points and leave room for surprise. A wishlist guides guests; it does not replace their judgment. Many people appreciate the clarity.

faqs.question: Can guests still pick something not on my wishlist?
faqs.answer: Of course. A wishlist is a helpful map, not a rulebook. Guests who know you well may go off-list — and that is fine.

faqs.question: How does WishGather improve a basic wishlist?
faqs.answer: Guests claim items privately so others see what is still available, product links import details when possible, and your list updates in real time — fewer duplicates and less awkward guesswork.

compare.title: WishGather vs Google Sheets for gift lists
compare.lead: Spreadsheets are flexible but fragile for group gifting. Here's how a purpose-built registry compares for privacy, mobile guests, and real-time updates.

sections.title: Privacy
sections.body: Sheets often show every guest name in column B. WishGather hides claimer names from other guests while giving the host full detail — better for showers, offices, and classroom parties.

sections.title: Mobile experience
sections.body: Pinching and zooming a spreadsheet on a phone frustrates guests. WishGather is a mobile-first guest page with large tap targets and clear Available badges.

sections.title: Real-time updates
sections.body: Sheets rely on manual edits and refresh. WishGather pushes claim changes live so two people rarely buy the same gift.

sections.title: Product details
sections.body: Paste a store link and WishGather can import title, image, and price. Sheets need copy-paste for every field unless you build formulas yourself.

faqs.question: When is a spreadsheet still fine?
faqs.answer: Tiny, trusted groups who do not mind visible names may prefer Sheets. For larger guest lists, WishGather reduces mistakes.

faqs.question: Can I export from WishGather?
faqs.answer: Yes. Download a PDF summary from your manage page after the event.

privacy.title: Your data, handled with care
privacy.lead: WishGather is built for private gifting. We collect only what's needed to run your registry and never sell guest information.
privacy.collectHosts: Hosts: name, email, and password (hashed) when you create an account.
privacy.collectGuests: Guests: first name when claiming a gift, plus an anonymous browser token so you can unclaim your own selection.
privacy.collectLists: Lists: gift titles, links, images, prices, and claim status.
privacy.visibilityText: On the public list, guests see whether each item is available or already selected. They do not see who claimed an item or when it was claimed. Only the list host sees claimer names and timestamps.
privacy.linksText: When you paste a product URL, our server fetches public product metadata (title, image, price) to populate your list. We do not store your shopping credentials or purchase history.
privacy.retentionText: Your lists and claims remain until you delete them or close your account. Guest tokens are stored in the browser's local storage on the guest's device.
privacy.questionsText: For privacy questions about your registry, contact the host who shared the list with you. Hosts manage their own gift lists and exported reports. See also our <cookieLink>Cookie Policy</cookieLink>.

cookies.title: How we use cookies and browser storage
cookies.lead: WishGather uses browser storage for sign-in and guest claims, and Google Analytics in production to understand how the site is used. We do not use advertising cookies.
cookies.whatText: Cookies are small text files stored by your browser. Similar technologies — such as local storage — can also save data on your device. This policy covers both cookies and the browser storage WishGather uses.
cookies.storageHost: Host login (local storage): When you sign in, your session token and basic profile are stored in local storage so you stay logged in on that browser.
cookies.storageGuest: Guest claims (local storage): When a guest claims a gift, an anonymous token is saved in local storage so they can unclaim their selection from the same browser.
cookies.analyticsText: We use Google Analytics (Google tag) on wishgather.com to collect aggregated usage data such as pages visited and general traffic patterns. Google may set cookies or use similar technologies. You can learn more in Google's privacy policy and use browser extensions or settings to opt out of Analytics.
cookies.notUsedText: WishGather does not set marketing or social-media advertising cookies. Host authentication is handled with a token in local storage, not a login cookie.
cookies.thirdPartyText: Gift lists may display product images loaded from retailer CDNs (for example Amazon or Next). Those providers may use their own cookies if you follow a product link to their site. Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts when you visit WishGather.
cookies.managingText: You can clear WishGather data by signing out (hosts), clearing site data in your browser settings, or using a private browsing window. Clearing storage will sign you out and remove guest claim tokens on that device.
cookies.moreText: For details on what personal data we collect and how it is used, see our <privacyLink>Privacy Policy</privacyLink>.
